evidenceAudit.scope: People living with advanced dementia: needs-based palliative care, distress and agitation, pain assessment, eating and drinking, and anticipatory planning. Verified against NICE NG97 and NG31; pain doses from MOH Protocol-010.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

pathophysiology.summary: Advanced dementia brings severe cognitive and functional decline, inability to communicate needs, swallowing difficulty and frailty. Progression is unpredictable, so palliative care should be offered from diagnosis (NICE NG97).
keyMechanisms: Neurodegeneration impairs memory, language and executive function; pain and discomfort may show only as behaviour change.
Swallowing difficulty causes aspiration and weight loss; tube feeding does not improve outcomes in severe dementia (NICE NG97).
Antipsychotics increase harm and can cause severe sensitivity reactions in Lewy body or Parkinson's dementia (NICE NG97).

symptoms: Agitation, distress, withdrawal, poor intake, sleep disturbance.
physicalSigns: Pain behaviours; weight loss; pressure areas; signs of infection or retention.
redFlags: Severe distress with risk to self or others
Unexplained behaviour change — check pain, delirium
precipitants: Alzheimer's, vascular, Lewy body or mixed dementia

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute change — look for infection, drugs, retention.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Moderate–severe dementia or unable to self-report; repeat after changes
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Stepwise analgesia; reassess after each intervention (NICE NG97 1.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Palliative approach
actions: Offer flexible, needs-based palliative care; anticipatory planning with person and family (NICE NG97 1.10).

clinicalManagement.title: Distress and agitation
actions: Assess and treat causes first; personalised activities.
Antipsychotic only if risk of harm or severe distress from agitation, hallucinations or delusions; lowest dose, shortest time, review every 6 weeks; stop if no clear benefit (NICE NG97).
Avoid in Lewy body/Parkinson's dementia where possible; no valproate for agitation.

clinicalManagement.title: Pain
actions: Stepwise analgesia — start with paracetamol (MOH Protocol-010 dose); reassess with observational tool.

clinicalManagement.title: Eating and drinking
actions: Support eating and drinking; SLT if unsafe; no routine enteral feeding (NICE NG97).

learningObjectives: Provide comfort-focused, needs-based care for people living with advanced dementia.
